newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni investors building 100,000 bpd refinery.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni investors building 100,000 bpd refinery.

text.p: Yemeni investors said on Wednesday they had laid the cornerstone for a 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) oil refinery, the first such private venture in the Arab state that has just one ageing refinery in Aden.

"The cornerstone for the project was laid on Tuesday," Abdul-Rab Senan, one of the investors, told Reuters. He said the refinery was located at Ras Isa in the province of Hudaidah, 226 km west of the Yemeni capital Sanaa.
He put the cost of the first phase at $250 million.
"That will reach $400 million in the second phase. The entire project will be finalised within a year to three years from now," Senan said.
Refining capacity will initially stand at 60,000 bpd, "which could rise to 100,000 bpd in the second phase."
Deputy oil minister Moheiddine Aldhabbi said the ministry had authorised the al-Hacheidi investment group, which comprises Yemeni investors and businessmen, to set up the refinery.
He said the group "will implement all the work of the project from start to finish without any government role."
Yemen is the Arab world's poorest country with a relatively low oil production of around 350,000 bpd.

Its only refinery in Aden has a design capacity of 170,000 bpd, but actually runs are limited to 100,000 bpd because of the age and configuration of the plant which was damaged during Yemen's 1994 civil war.
Yemeni oil sources said last month the country was studying a proposal to build a new crude distillation unit (CDU) alongside the existing 42-year-old refinery site.
